This system enables us to not only measure the concentration of biological target molecules but also determine the hydrodynamic parameters of the sample. For example, we can measure viscosity, diffusion coefficients, and blood coagulation reaction rates in the fluidic device within a few seconds.

articleTitle: Real-time microscopic video shooting using a view-expanded microscope system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This study proposes a real-time video shooting system using a view-expanded microscope. The proposed system composed of a microscope, a galvanometer mirror and a high-speed vision system is capable of obtaining a 16,000×2,000 pixel microscopic image in real time at 25 fps by combining multiple visual fields. The effectiveness of our system is demonstrated through video shooting experiments of moving sea urchin embryos in a microchannel.

articleTitle: Microfluidic liquid cell in scanning electron microscope for visualization of in-liquid living cell
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Drug resistant bacteria appear and have the risks for the wide spread around the world. The development of new antibacterial agents is emergently required, though it is difficult due to the lack of methods to find new action mechanisms of antibacterial agents. High resolution imaging with material mapping is one of the good approaches to find new action mechanisms for antibacterial agents. We developed microfluidic liquid cell which visualizes cellular morphology and material distribution using a scanning electron microscope (SEM) and refluxes cell culture medium without any liquid leakage inside the SEM. Further, a cell culture chamber inside the SEM was also developed and could maintain the cell cultural condition. The combination of the liquid cell and the chamber achieved the visualization of in-liquid objects under controlled environment by using SEM. As a demonstration, we observed that a couple of bubbles flew through a microchannel from an observation window of the liquid cell where an 80-nm-thick silicon nitride membrane was suspended.

articleTitle: Fabrication of three-dimensional deformable microfilter for capturing target cells
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This paper presents a three-dimensional deformable microfilter modified with a nucleic-acid aptamer for capturing of target cells. Separating and capturing target cells from the fluid is very important for health diagnosis and medical diagnosis by liquid biopsy. The presented microfilter permits the separation of arbitrary size because the opening gap of the microfilter is three-dimensionally transformed by fluidic force. The deformation of the microfilter is able to be changed by adjusting the fluidic force. Also, the presented microfilter permits the specific capturing of target cells by specifically adsorbing ability of a nucleic-acid aptamer. In this experiment, the cancer cell was used as a target cell. The nucleic-acid aptamer that has a specific adsorbing ability to epithelial cell adhesion molecules was used for capturing the cancer cell. The results of experiment, the target cells were effectively captured by nucleic-acid aptamer modified microfilter.

articleTitle: Improvement of 3D reconstruction image by confocal microscope with cell rotated
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: The goal of this research is to construct a high resolution 3D image in all directions of XYZ with the small micro hand system with 4 degrees of freedom including rotation.

articleTitle: Estimation of hemiplegia by gripping force distribution
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Is this study, to assist walking motion for elderly people and disabled people, robotics-based assist technologies are important. Toward to realize such technologies, we have developed cane-type walking assist robot. In this paper, in order to establish a method to estimate the posture of the operator from the distribution information of the force applied to the handle of the robot, a preliminary experiment is performed to detect the presence or absence of hemiplegia of the operator.

articleTitle: Electrical stimulation for compensation of impaired lower limb sensation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This paper proposes an electrical stimulation method that provides a movement trajectory feedback for paraplegic patients who lost the sensory function of lower body. The paraplegic patient is completely or partially lost the motor or sensory function of lower legs due to spinal cord injury. Wearable robotic exoskeletons apply torques on hip and knee joints to enable the paraplegic patient walk again. The electrical stimulation integrates 55 stimulation points, which 22 are stimulation point and 33 are ground points. These stimulation points are fitted into a coordinate and projected onto a plane space. The effectiveness of the electric stimulation is verified through a `trajectory reproduction' experiment. The experiment result shows a certain accuracy of the proposed electrical stimulation pattern.

articleTitle: Gait diagnosis for elderly people to prevent fall and development of training assist tool using augmented reality
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Recently, the population ratio of elderly people in Japan is increasing rapidly. In order to improve and maintain the quality of life of the elderly people, preventing `fall' is very important social issue. In our research, we proposed a gait measurement and diagnosis system which can automatically analyze and clarify the gait condition of each elderly by using measured feature values. And we proposed a training assist tool using the augmented reality for better gait training. From the experimental results, it turned out that the person with the relatively high risk of fall has a low balancing ability. Therefore, in order to prevent elderly people's fall, it is necessary to grasp their own gait condition properly and to maintain and improve balancing ability by the appropriate training or exercise.

articleTitle: Pulse wave measurement using wide range load sensor using quartz crystal resonator
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This paper reports on an unrestricted pulse wave measurement system not depending on individual difference and sitting condition. As an aging society has grown, it has been more and more important to measure biological signals in daily life. We have succeeded in measuring pulse, respiration and body movement in beds and chairs by wide range load sensor using quartz crystal resonator (QCR). However, it is occasionally difficult to detect pulse waves during the objects sitting on chairs because of changes in the contact condition due to individual differences and sitting condition. Therefore, we propose the pulse wave measurement system using multiple load sensors to resolve these problems. By selecting the sensor that has appropriate contact condition from several sensors, the measurement accuracy can be impoved. In addition, to select the sensor, we defined peak index that indicate the accuracy of the measurement and verified the feasibility.

articleTitle: Hydrogel fluorescent sensor for long term environmental measurement
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Long-term environment measurement by hydrogel fluorescence sensor using fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) was developed. Photobleaching of fluorescence sensor is compensated by FRAP in the fluorescence sensor made of low concentration of polyethyleneglycol diacrylate (PEG-DA). Effectiveness of the fluorescence sensor was confirmed by temperature calibration, time-course monitoring of fluorescence, and temperature measurement by the fluorescence sensor.

articleTitle: Transparent printhead for transporting multiple micro-droplets
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Parallelized manipulation of single cells encapsulated in micro-droplets has been demanded. This paper reports the fabrication of a printhead for transporting multiple micro-droplets. The head was composed of a PDMS chip and a SU-8 substrate with openings. These two parts were bonded after nitrogen plasma treatment of PDMS. We characterized the fabricated chip. Fluorescence particles were injected to the nozzle array. We evaluated transport property through the nozzle array.

articleTitle: The topographical switching of focal adhesion maturation sites and actin filament activation on the well-defined grid micropatterns
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Securing robust cell adhesion between cells and biomaterials is one of key considerations for tissueengineering. However, the cell adhesion investigation by the biophysical effects such as topography or rigidity of substrates has only been recently reported. In this study, we examined the spatial property of focal adhesions by changing the height of micropatterns in two kinds of microtopography (grid and post) and the stiffness of the substrates. We found that the focal adhesion localization is highly regulated by topographical variation (height) of gird micropattens but not the rigidity of substrates or the function of actin cytoskeleton, although the latters strongly influence the focal adhesion size or area. In detail, the change of the height of the grid micropatterns results in the switching of focal adhesion sites; as the height increases, the localization of focal adhesion is switched from top to bottom areas. This study demonstrates that the localization of focal adhesion on well-defined micropatterned substrates is critically determined by the topographical variation in the micropatterns.

articleTitle: Autonomous mowing robot using a tracking laser rangefinder
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: We are developing an autonomous mowing robot. GPS is used for identifying the self-location of the robot outdoors. GPS cannot be used when the radio wave for GPNN signals from satellites are shut off by mountains, and buildings. Therefore, we have developed an instrument that measures the position of a robot instead of GPS. The instrument is named the tracking laser rangefinder. We made prototype autonomous mobile mowing robot with the laser rangefinder. We made performance tests on autonomous locomotion using an experimental vehicle, but the tracking accuracy to the target path was insufficient.

articleTitle: Mechanical characterization of a single synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 cell in different osmolarity solutions
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: We report the evaluation results of Young's modulus of single Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 cell in normal and high osmolarity conditions. The measurement is realized by using a microfluidic chip on a microscope with an optical tweezers system. The Young's modulus is measured by compressing the cell and measure the deformation and cellular reactive force. We measured wild type cells and showed the difference of Young's Modulus of single cell in different osmolarity conditions.

articleTitle: Measurement of two- and three-dimensional viscoelasticity of tissue and artificial organ
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In recent years, researches are being carried out on the creating of surgical simulators for brain subjects, aimed at surgical training of young physicians. Also, based on the creating of the brain surgery simulator, not only the creating of tissue models such as dura mater, brain, and tumor, but also their evaluation becomes important. Living tissue has both elasticity and viscosity, and by evaluating both, it will evaluate the mechanical properties.

articleTitle: Development of multi-organs-on-a-chip mimicking physiological parameters: Evaluation of the function using prodrug CPT-11
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this study, we developed a microfluidic device with metabolism function during pharmacokinetic study. We reproduced physiological parameters such as an organ volume ratio and a blood flow ratio on the device. The ratios are replicated by area of cell culture chambers and a bypass channel. HepG2 (Metabolism Model) and A549 (Target Cancer Cells) were co-cultured in each culture chambers in the device. Then we performed cell-based assays using an anticancer drug model (CPT-11) and an antihyperlipidemic drug model (Simvastatin). As a result, A549 cells density in the case of CPT-11 and Simvastatin exposure decreased due to inhibit Carboxylesterase metabolism by Simvastatin. We conclude that the device can be applied to the evaluation of complicated metabolism function in human body.

articleTitle: Real-time in situ observation of immature bone tissue subjected to mechanical loading in culture
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: It is well known that bones in the body respond to mechanical loading by maintaining or altering their structure and subsequently stiffness and strength. In particular, this process is important in the development and the maturation of skeletal tissues, as the loading stimulates bone matrix synthesis and subsequent tissue calcification. However, how mechanical loading stimulates bone calcification and how the calcification progresses within the bone tissue remains unknown. The purpose of the present study was, therefore, to investigate how the calcification of immature bone tissue is stimulated by mechanical loading. A new experimental system was developed for real-time microscopic observation of bone tissue calcification in culture environment. We used bone explants, with a thickness of 200 p, m, obtained from 2- to 4-day-old chick tibia, and observed the specimen under 10% static tensile strain during 24 h. It was demonstrated that tissue calcification progressed slowly at a constant rate in the sample subjected to 0% strain (no strain controls). By contrast, the calcification was accelerated between 13 h and 20 h in strained samples, resulting in significantly larger calcified area. In addition, it was observed that the calcification progressed mainly to the direction of the applied tensile strain. The present study has demonstrated that bone calcification was stimulated in the presence of static tensile strain, and the calcification progressed to the strain direction. This may be attributable to that collagen fibers in uncalcified region were realigned to the strain direction, and the realigned fiber structure enhanced transport of osteogenic factors to augment the calcification of the fibers.

articleTitle: Remote control console of mowing robot with image monitor
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This paper describes our developed remote operator console with an image monitor for a weed mowing robot. The console is Tablet PC (Personal Computer). The operator moves the mowing robot while watching the camera images and touching the buttons in GUI (Graphical User Interface). Using the remote operator console, we were able to operate the weed mowing robot from the shade of 30m away.

articleTitle: Magnetic self-assembly of toroidal microstructures by shaking
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this paper, we conducted self-assembly of magnetized hydrogels by shaking. The magnetized toroidal microstructures were assembled automatically to form tube structures using magnetic force. The shaking speed was experimentally optimized to achieve high speed and longer tube assembly. The assembly of toroidal microstructures to form tube structures was achieved. The particle image velocimetry (PIV) experiments were conducted to check flow velocity inside a dish during assembly process. The method we conducted can be applied to assemble 3D cell structures with vascular-like channels for tissue engineering applications.

articleTitle: Fabrication of hollow branch structure without core by circumferential exposure for vascular model with temperature indicating function
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this study, we proposed new fabrication method of hollow branch vascular model by circumferential exposure to improve the uniformity of vascular model without core as shown in Fig. 1. A schematic diagram of fabrication process is shown in Fig. 2. Main constitute of vascular model is polyethylene glycol diacrylate (PEG-DA), polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), distilled water, and temperature indicator dye as shown in table 1. PEG-DA is hydrophilic cross-linkable resin. First, outer mold is fabricated by transparent and oxygen permeable material like polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). Then, material is introduced and ultraviolet (UV) light is illuminated from circumference. The material is polymerized from outside. After UV illumination, uncured resin is removed. Finally, the fabricated vascular model is extracted by detachment of outer mold. Thickness of the vascular model is controlled by UV illumination time.

articleTitle: Non-contact wettability assessment for detecting cellular behaviors
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This study aimed to detect the behavior of cultivated cells such as cell differentiation via the surface wettability. The surface wettability on cultivated cells was assessed by air-jet based liquid squeezing method, where the liquid squeezed diameter was used for an index of surface wettability. The wettability of normal mouse skeletal myoblast cell line C2C12 was lower than that of myogenic-differentiated C2C12 cells. This result suggested a potential to detect cell differentiation via surface wettability.

articleTitle: Latest data processing technologies for living state estimation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this paper, image and point cloud processing methods for food volume estimation are introduced. By using a depth/thermal camera, it can be estimated even in difficult situations with a color camera. With the methods, a home robot can predict the end of meals based on the change in volume and deliver a dose of medicines after meals.

articleTitle: Wireless remote control for a vibration-driven electromagnet-type moving microrobot (Fabrication of third prototype microrobot and experimental results for straight running and turning)
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In recent years, various investigations have been conducted on microrobots by many researchers, and contests are held throughout the year with the aim of developing microrobot technologies. As a result, various types of microrobots have been proposed including motor-type, piezoelectric-element-type, and electromagnet-type microrobots. To date, the author's research group has been studying a locomotion mechanism and a control method for an electromagnet-type microrobot, which has a volume of 1cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. In a previous study by the author, a structure and a control method that enable a microrobot with only one electromagnet coil to turn were proposed, and the characteristics of a running microrobot were investigated through some experiments. However, the developed microrobot could not move freely because of the wires which supply energy or control signals from the battery and the controller. To date, I proposed the wireless remote control method for a microrobot and developed the first and second prototype wireless remote controlled microrobot and performed some experiments to confirm the proposed method. In this paper, I fabricated third prototype microrobot and carried out some experiments on its straight running and turning.

articleTitle: Micro/nano-scale needle devices for the brain
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This paper reports our recent progresses on silicon growth technology-based micro-/nano-scale three-dimensional (3D) needle-electrode array devices, for use in electrophysiological recordings of neurons/cells within the brain tissue.

articleTitle: All-in-one bag based photooxidative cell membrane perforation system for mass cell processing
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In recent years, cell processing technology has evolved in the advanced medical field, and the processed cells are applied to various diseases which hardly be treated. In order to treat these diseases, the cells must have the functions which are necessary for the treatment. However, it's difficult to add some artificial functions to cells, such as drug delivery Our photochemical cell membrane perforation is an new approach for the cell processing. This method allows a large number of cells to perforate recoverable holes on cell membranes with a nano brush shaped stamp including photosensitizer and light irradiation to activate the photosensitizer. Advantages of the method are as follows: The number of processed cells can be increased easily because our stamp-based cell processing is like a printing technology, and survival ratio of the processed cell are fundamentally high since the perforation is based on recoverable oxidative damages to the cells.

articleTitle: Multisensory alterations in visual, vestibular and proprioceptive cues for modeling of postural control
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In sensory inputs of postural control, visual and vestibular inputs, as well as both proprioceptive and tactile somatosensory inputs, are required to control posture-regulating muscles in the whole body, especially in the lower limbs and trunk. Changes in multisensory inputs elicit appropriate changes immediately in posture corresponding to the sensory information. Because the central nerve system is complex, the mechanism by which this regulation occurs is still unknown. In this study, we set up experiments with measurements of muscular activities by multisensory alterations to investigate the tonus control in postural control. We focus on visual, vestibular and proprioceptive sensations in this paper. From the results of the positions and the standard deviations of CoPs, we confirm that the experiments were well-done to our aim. In the standard deviations of CoPs, the effects of instability rise up in the order of GVS, closed eyes and vibration. However, it is interesting that these are not simple summation but with something to be integrated. From the result of EMGs, comparing with control conditions, almost muscular activities rise up in several conditions. However, it is difficult to find regularity between sensations and muscular activities. We should continue to analyze the results for our hypothesis.

articleTitle: Simultaneous printing of multiple origami structures
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: We developed a self-folding method of a printed paper. The paper self-folds along the printed line with a desktop inkjet printer to get 3D structure. In this paper, we introduce a method to fabricate multiple 3D structures simultaneously. Multiple development designs were arranged on A4 sized paper, and the A4 sized paper is printed to self-fold multiple developments. The proposed method has an advantage especially in small scale, because when design of the development is smaller, more numbers of structures can place in A4 sized paper and construct. Plenty of small and light 3D structures are fabricated simultaneously with low-cost. The feature has good affinity with swarm robotics, and many paper robots may locomote using their own structural intelligence obtained by the self-folding.

articleTitle: Cooperative monitoring multiple humans using UAVs and fixed camera
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: The cooperative monitoring system using UAVs and fixed cameras is proposed for monitoring multiple humans in a particular area. In the proposed system, the UAVs pursue the humans who are not photographed by the fixed cameras to identify them. Fort the efficient pursuit, observation points of UAVs should be minimized. Based on the Image Information Added Map, the observation area for a person is determined. As for the necessary condition, one picture for each person should be taken. The optimization problem is solved by a set covering problem. The proposed algorithm is implemented on simulation and simulation results are shown.

articleTitle: Size effect on crack propagation of nano-scale silicon with different type of nothes
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This study reports our two unpredictable behaviors for fracture of nano-scale silicon with 100 nm thickness. We developed a novel tensile testing method conducted on silicon chip to observe a local area in large magnified view during tensile test. For comparing fracture behavior of 100 nm-thick silicon film with V-notch and U-notch, we performed FEM analysis to optimize the locations of notches. The results shows that V-notch generating large local stress-field at a notch root was stronger for tensile stress than U-notch.

articleTitle: Direct observation and behavior analysis of Enchytraeus japonensis in soft material for swarm intelligent micro robots
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this study, we report the observation and behavior analysis of Enchytraeus japonensis, a species of earthworm, as the first step for creating swarm intelligent micro robots. Several studies have been conducted on the earthworm's behaviors of constructing tunnels by biologists and agronomists. Earthworms make intricate network of tunnels in the soil. We presumed that earthworms use self-organization to make this intricate structure, and we investigated the Enchytraeus japonensis's behaviors. Two experiments to observe their behaviors and to confirm construction of tunnels with self-organization were done. As the results, we observed that their behaviors were both tracking the same direction with other individuals, and changing direction with sensing the surrounding environments of hardness. These behaviors emerge the intricate network of tunnels with self-organization.

articleTitle: 3D pH measurement for cell culture using CT scan
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In cell culture, the pH of culture liquid is one of the most important conditions. However, culture liquid may have pH-gradient due to the activity of cells and change of the environment. In order to confirm the existence of pH-gradient, we propose a method for 3D pH measurement using the color change of phenol red. Using the principle of CT scan, we can measure pH-gradient without contacting culture liquid, and thus, decrease the possibility of contamination. In this paper, we consider the influence of light refraction by a cylindrical vessel, and show that we can measure local pH of culture liquid by light absorbance.

articleTitle: In vitro mimic of hepatic lobule tissue using ca-alginate cell-containing hydrogel modules
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This paper reported a cell system that fabricate alginate gel cell sheets with flat surface for assembly of multilayered hepatic lobule model based on electrodeposition. The centimeter-scale cell sheets were produced with pre-designed hepatic lobule patterns. After a one-day culture, we successfully detached the sheets from the 2D electrode substrate without any structural defect and stacked them into 3D multilayer hepatic lobule tissue within a PDMS mold. Cell proliferation and viability of long-term survival were quantitatively measured because this is the need for three-dimensional liver systems used in pharmacological tests. This study aims to clarify that alginate cell sheets created by electrodeposition can potentially be utilized for 3D tissue constructs.

articleTitle: A design strategy of a bioreactor for platelet production using fluid force
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this study, we showed that platelets were produced from megakaryocytes using a bioreactor with a slope shaped 3D microchannel by applying fluid force. In previous studies, slit structures have been utilized to produce platelets in a microfluidic chip. However, it is difficult to trap megakaryocytes of various size by using the pre-patterned slit structures. Therefore, we present a bioreactor which can trap various size of megakaryocytes. In this study, we constructed a bioreactor with a slope shaped 3D microchannel, and succeed in on-chip platelet production.

articleTitle: Olfactory cues to enhance simultaneous motor learning in opposing force fields
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Simultaneous learning of two contradicting motor tasks (i.e. tasks with opposing force fields) has been reported to be difficult. Osu et al. (2004) [11] revealed that such dual learning is achieved by attributing different contextual cues to each motor task (e.g. displaying a red color during motor task A and a blue color during moto task B). Based on this previous study, we aimed to study whether olfactory stimuli can serve as contextual cues. We conducted behavioral experiments in which the participants were required to learn arm-reaching tasks in unfamiliar force fields. As contextual cues, we used odors of lemon and lavender, which have opposing functions: Lemon is believed to enhance mental or physical task performance, while lavender is considered to be a relaxant. Our results showed that lemon odors reduced the number of errors after learning contradicting motor tasks, while lavender did not. This suggests that specific olfactory cues can serve as contextual cues to promote the simultaneous learning of contradicting motor tasks.

articleTitle: Design framework of robot-assisted therapy for children with autism
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Use of robots in socially assistive tasks is dynamically growing. Robot-assisted therapy for children with autism is one of the most popular practical applications. Design of robot-assisted therapy requires intensive effort on close collaboration with experts in the related fields for effective therapeutic interventions. At the same time, in-depth analysis for autism therapy session and theoretical background and careful consideration in easy rapid application are importantly necessary because the end user of robot is autism therapist after all.

articleTitle: Vividness control of KI with variations in visual stimulus patterns
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: We develop a new rehabilitation device that combines the effects of two illusions: the kinesthetic illusion (KI) and the rubber hand illusion (RHI). We investigate whether KI can be reinforced with RHI where the former is caused by applying the oscillator's vibration to the flexor carpi radialis muscle (FCR) of a right hand. RHI is caused by showing moving images of a right hand overlapped on the subject's hand through a display pad. The illusion's vividness is induced in the right hand was represented by the left hand and measured by a rotary encoder, which can measure the joint angle of the flexion and the extension motion of the right wrist. We conducted experiments that quantitatively compared the KI strength that was reinforced by the visual stimulus with the pure KI strength, where the enhanced KI strength was about 1.4 to 1.5 times stronger than the unenhanced KI.

articleTitle: Possibilities of mammalian cell preservation using freeze-dried methods
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In general, mammalian somatic cells are preserved in the ultra low temperature freezer or the liquid nitrogen. However, the maintenance and transportation of frozen cells are costly, and there are problems with a safety aspect on liquid nitrogen. Freeze drying, which removes moisture through sublimation, has been used for a long-term storage of food, drug, yeast. To our knowledge, little work has been devoted to freeze dry for mammalian cells. The objective of this study was to establish a FD method to preserve mammalian spermatozoa and somatic cells, and to suggest the future technology for genetic preservation.

articleTitle: Imaging method of oocyte by using a micro-scale rotational flow
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this paper, we report an imaging method of a single oocyte by using a micro-scale rotational flow. This method gently and indirectly rotates the target oocyte to obtain surface images in 0.176 s. The necessary equipment for this method is only a syringe pump and microfluidic chip with single 40 μm diameter orifice.

articleTitle: Fabrication of glass-based bio-chip utilizing ultrashort-pulse-laser and its application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Ultrashort-pulse-laser known as femtosecond (fs) laser has been widely applied in various fields such as electrical, chemical, cell biology and microfluidics researches since the tightly focused fs laser enables 3 dimensional (3D) microfabrication inside the transparent materials. Over the last decades, many research groups have exploited the 3D fs laser processing of the transparent materials from the point of fundamental researches and industrial applications. In this presentation, we discuss recent development of the 3D fs laser fabrication of microfluidics and some other optical components to be integrated to the microfluidic chip. Furthermore, applications of the fs laser fabricated microfluidic chips will be presented in the talk.

articleTitle: Non natural tiny-wet machine: Molecular robot
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: The realization of a tiny-wet machine assembled from the molecular devices such as sensors, actuators, and even logic circuits is one of the major goals of the bioinspired micro-nano robotics. We constructed an ameba-like molecular robot capable of expressing continuous shape change in response to specific signal molecules [1]. The robot includes a main body, an actuator, and an actuator control device (molecular clutch). When the clutch was engaged, the robot showed continuous shape change. When the clutch was disconnected, the shape change behavior stopped. These results show that the components of the robot are consistently integrated into the functional system. We are expecting that this research can provide a platform for constructing increasingly complex and functional molecular systems with controllable motility.

articleTitle: Fine processing of polymer surface by irradiating local atmospheric pressure plasma jets using helium source gas mixed with water vapor
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Atmospheric pressure plasma jets (APPJ) have attracted much attention in recent years because it can be driven under atmospheric pressure. We have developed an ultrafine APPJ processing technique using a nanopipette that is a tapered glass capillary with an aperture of submicometer or smaller in diameter. The nanopipette was used not only as a nozzle for localized APPJ generation but also as a probe for scanning probe microscopy. By using the technique, fine processing of a photoresist film was achieved with a submicrometer resolution. However, the processing rate was low, and applicable materials for the fabrication were limited. In this paper, to improve the etching rate and versatility of the applicable materials, we developed a fabrication method using hydroxyl radicals by adding water vapor to the plasma source gas. The fabrication properties of polymethyl methacrylate using the proposed method were investigated.

articleTitle: Liquid junction potential in the pH measurement and microfluidic pH measurement device using ISFET sensor
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: We investigate a liquid junction (LJ) used in the reference electrode for potentiometry. The LJ device is essential in the pH measurement using glass electrode or ion-sensitive field-effect transistor (ISFET). Though traditional and reliable, the conventional LJ devices have some unsolved problems. First, we explain about a common type LJ device, then reconsider two types of pH measurement device we have previously reported, next consider a new LJ device using ISFET sensors.

articleTitle: Microfluidic device for applying a mechanical stimulus to a large number of cellular nuclei
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This paper reports on development and improvement of a microfluidic device applying the mechanical stimulus to numerous cellular nuclei. Many researches have reported that the mechanical stimulus is important factor of cellular differentiation. But, It is not clearly understood what effects mechanical stimulus induce to cellular nuclei. Our purpose is to reveal the effect by gene assay. For this purpose, we develop a microfluidic device by which we can apply a mechanical stimulus to cellular nuclei. In improvement, we conduct effective modification to the device for getting more cells and succeed in collecting over 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> cells. In experiment, we observe both deformation of cells and nuclei simultaneously and get preliminary result of gene expression about canceration.

articleTitle: Spatial and temporal correlation of muscle synergies in human walk-run transition
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Humans change gait depending on moving speed from walking to running and from running to walking. However, it remains unclear what mechanisms contribute to the gait transition. In this study, we performed singular value decomposition (SVD) analysis on the EMG data measured in human walk-run transition (WRT) and run-walk transition (RWT) to investigate the gait transition mechanism from a viewpoint of muscle synergy. Our results suggest that humans have an unique step at the gait transitions, whose spatial and temporal patterns are similar to those for running.

articleTitle: Micro folding structure using Ti-Ni-Zr high formable shape memory alloys
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this study, we proposed the fabrication process of the micro folding structures such as foldable pipe structures using Ti-Ni-Zr high formable shape memory alloys (HFSMAs). We investigated microforming ability, shape memory behaviors of Ti<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">38</sub>Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub>Zr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> (at.%) HFSMAs. We succeeded to fabricate folded samples without crystallization. Their folding angles 0were approximately 60° and 90°. Finally, folded samples were annealed at 873 K for 1 hour, and then they became SMAs. To investigate their shape memory behaviors, bending tests during several thermal cycles were conducted. As these results, both folded samples showed good shape memory behaviors, and could recover their initial shapes without plastic deformation, even if they were deformed to straight shape (0=180°).

articleTitle: Instantaneous acquisition of focused image using high-speed microscope system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a system in which a vibration machine is attached to the object lens of a microscope for moving the focus position rapidly by vibrating it up and down, in order to capture well-focused images based on edge strength information. An algorithm for capturing well-focused images based on edge strength information is implemented in the proposed system, and image capturing experiments are conducted for micro objects. The experimental results verify the effectiveness of our system, which captures well-focused images of high-speed micro moving objects.

articleTitle: Calcium signaling response of osteoblastic cells received with compressive stimuli
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This paper presents the evaluation of osteoblastic cell calcium signaling responses that received with compressive stimuli by fabricated microdevice. This microdevice was constructed by stacking of two PDMS structural layers. The compressive stimulus to cells can be controlled by regulating the expansion of the diaphragm via a pneumatic pressure to the device. In this experiment, compressive stimulus was gradually applied to the cells from 0-12 kPa. As a result, calcium signaling response of the center of cell and the edge of cell showed different behavior. In addition, when the compressive pressure became the 1.5 kPa, the calcium concentration of edge of cell was drastically increased. These results suggested that there is a threshold for the compressive stimulus received by the cells.

articleTitle: Development of accuracy evaluation system for multi-copter autonomous flight
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Our research group corresponds to rapid deterioration for infrastructure, we has been developing the autonomous flight of the multi-copter using position sensors. This paper is the purpose of development of accuracy evaluation system for multi-copter autonomous flight.

articleTitle: Open-window in microfluidic chip with ultra-thin glass for single cell isolation femtosecond laser irradiation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: An explosion phenomenon is induced in micrometer scale by focusing a femtosecond laser pulse in an aqueous solution. We have proposed to apply the explosion as an impulsive force to isolate cells flowing in a microfluidic chip. In this study, we fabricated a microfluidic chip with an open-window to isolate cells flowing in the chip channel and demonstrated the femtosecond laser-induced isolation of single micro polymer bead as a cell model. The microfluidic chip was composed of a bottom-open channel made of PDMS rubber and a 10 μm] thick ultra-thin glass as the bottom cover layer. The open-window was fabricated at the ultra-thin glass layer by scanning an intense focused femtosecond laser under microscope. In the microchip, polymer beads with 10 [μm] diameter in water buffer was injected with 0.1 [m/s] velocity. The flow stability in the channel on the top of the open-window was checked by high-speed imaging of the flowing beads. We focused the intense femtosecond laser into the channel on the top of the open-window intermittently, and attempted the laser-induced liquid drop injection from the open-window. The amount of the injected liquid was monitored by fluorescence dye dissolved in the water buffer. The result implied that the amount depended on the laser intensity for the laser cutting of the open-window. The laser intensity would relate with the wettability of the open-widow edge, which was speculated from the observation result of the window edge by scanning electronic microscopy. Finally, we demonstrated the laser-induced bead injection from the open window made by optimized fabrication condition, and indicated that single micro polymer bead could be isolated by the new methodology.

articleTitle: Hydrogel microfibers for biochemical applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This paper describes fabrication and applications of stimuli-responsive hydrogel microfibers for biochemical sensors and actuators. Our group has developed stimuli-responsive hydrogel microsprings (SR springs) for mugnifying the shrink/swell movements. The SR springs, made of composite hydrogel of p(NIPAM-co-AAc) and calcium alginate, were continuously formed by using a bevel-tip capillary. By stimulating single-layered or patterned SR springs, we achieved to magnify the shrink/swell movements and to control the direction of the movements.

articleTitle: Simultaneous observation of cell behavior on multiple substrates with different heights
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: We propose a microscopic system that can perform simultaneous time-lapse recordings for studying cell behavior on different substrates. The microscopic objective lens is controlled up and down so that the focal plane is matched with different heights of each surface. The captured video includes two types of images with a given time interval. Later, the focused image corresponding to each substrate is rearranged every time segment. To confirm the working principle, we show the experimental results for smooth muscle cells (SMCs) by using two different substrates.

articleTitle: Telebiometric system for infant and toddler fingerprint recognition
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Immunization and vaccination are very important for infant and toddler. The management system for registration in formal institution is not built yet. To overcome this problem, infant and toddler recognition using fingerprint can be chosen to identify infant and toddler. In this paper, we proposed a telebiometric system for infant and toddler recognition. The proposed system has three main components, namely sensor, mobile phone or PC, and server. The system used some feature extraction methods, such as ridge period, singular point, and minutiae, as fingerprint features to match it with the database data. The result showed that the system has 0.82 accuracy and 321 ms average running time.

articleTitle: Ground contact detection of robot legs by discriminating angular velocities and motor current
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: We investigated the contact detection method of legs using an angular velocity (AV) sensor and a current sensor. When lifted legs step on an obstacle, the AV of the robot body shows different patterns from the one of normal walking. Discriminating these unusual patterns from normal one, the robot control system is able to detect stepping on an obstacle. We experimented stepping on an obstacle and recorded the change of AVs. A three layered neural network was used for discrimination. As a result, a detection rate of 96 [%] was obtained. Referring the results of detection, the incline of robot body was suppressed to 1.0 [degree] by stopping the leg when it touched an obstacle. We also measured the motor current when a free leg stepped on an obstacle. The incline of robot body was suppressed to 0.7 [degree] or less at the detection rate of 100 [%].

articleTitle: Energy consumption evaluation of a lower limb active orthosis using stochastic analysis
publicationTitle: 2017 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This work presents an method to estimate the usage of energy consumption over time in electric actuators of an active orthosis, based on the concepts of stochastic processes. The presented method can be also applied in actuators of robotic manipulators. Active orthosis are robotic devices that assist people with some degree of the spinal cord injury. Active orthoses generally control the hip and knee joints movements through mechanical and electrical actuators. In some cases the device give the user the ability to select any desired movement, such as walking, sitting and standup, up and down stairs. For the most efficient execution of these movements it is important to analyse the evolution or estimate the energy consumption. For this, a board with Hall effect current sensors was used to acquire the data measured at each instant of the actuators. In addition, it is necessary to observe how energy is distributed in the frequency domain, and how its spectral density analysis is performed. The proposed work reinforces the importance of energy consumption analysis of rotational electric actuators that are responsible for driving the joints movements of lower limbs active orthosis.
